humor.style: self-deprecating - often makes fun of himself or his situation

humor.mechanism: understatement - often downplays situations for comedic effect

structural_patterns: frequently uses 'as you know' to preface explanations

uses 'let me tell you' before sharing personal stories

worldview.perception of authority: views authority figures with skepticism, often questioning their decisions - another character might show more deference or respect

self_image_vs_reality.self_image: sees himself as a laid-back, humorous guy who just wants to enjoy work

self_image_vs_reality.gap_behavior: uses humor to deflect from his dissatisfaction, often making jokes about his situation

emotional_tells.when_guarded: speaks in a light, joking manner, masking deeper feelings of frustration
emotional_tells.when_genuinely_afraid: speech becomes more staccato, with shorter sentences and a higher pitch
emotional_tells.when_grieving_or_defeated: speech compresses to simple, direct statements, often lacking his usual humor
emotional_tells.when_in_control: displays confidence through assertive speech, often making jokes that highlight his dominance in the conversation

situational_behavior.when_outmatched: uses banter to deflect tension, and if that fails, he may retreat or go silent
situational_behavior.when_disagreeing_with_authority: questions their decisions with humor, often undermining their authority subtly
situational_behavior.when_someone_they_protect_is_at_risk: becomes more serious and direct, showing a protective instinct
situational_behavior.when_proven_wrong: often redirects the conversation or makes a joke to deflect from the mistake

escalation_pattern: starts with humor to ease tension, escalates to sarcasm if ignored, and may become frustrated if not taken seriously
